Jev 1.13.0 · Eval only · 23 September 2026

Which changes can we leave out of review?

A larger, history-based experiment varies the prompt, source metadata, probability rule, threshold, and token window together. False exclusions come first; useful review work avoided per request comes next.

What this run found

“False exclusion” means hiding a changed line the reviewer wants to see. Zero observed errors is evidence from this corpus, not a guarantee about future changes.

The annotation erratum from the first run

The original audit missed two attributes on a test-only module: #[cfg(all(test, unix))] and its #[path]. They are outside your review scope. An additional GPT-6-sol audit checked this error class across all 180 cases and confirmed exactly two corrections.

Validation metrics apply this documented erratum to each run's frozen finalists. Their order is determined only by development scores. Scores against the original labels remain visible. The timed rerun uses fresh API responses with the same corpus and known corrections; it is not a new independent holdout.

Scores against original labels and source-backed erratum


First, make the labels defensible


Actual repository history
Each fixture records its commit, original path, exact diff, and a category/reason for every changed old and new line.


Source-assisted annotation
Rust syntax supplies initial labels. Three GPT‑6‑sol agents at medium effort audited separate 60-case batches, using historical module owners and callers where needed. The initial 36 corrections were applied before inference; the later two-line erratum is disclosed above.


A separate validation set
Adjacent groups of three commits stay together. Exact duplicate changed-text payloads are removed. Related lines and hunks remain correlated; this is one repository, not an independent multi-project benchmark.


Your policy excludes comments, imports/re-exports/module declarations, formatting, tests, prose docs, generated output and lockfiles. Runtime code, attributes, configuration, strings and embedded agent instructions remain significant. Mixed targets must stay in review.


Annotation corrections and limits


Full line labels · Audit evidence




Three factors, one frozen experiment


Prompt and metadata
Terse policy, structured checklist, contrastive examples, or category questions. Each sees rows alone; rows plus path/language; or those fields plus old/new file headers.


Decision rule
Choice probability, margin, confidence gates, probability × confidence; category max, clipped sum, noisy-or, a review veto, or the complement of “requires review.” Thresholds span 0.50–0.995, plus an argmax control.


Token window
4k, 8k, 12k, 16k and 20k estimated tokens: 12.5–62.5% of the nominal 32k state-plus-longest-question limit. Full hunks first, recursive midpoint splits if needed, then as much neighboring context as the budget permits.


The same Rust splitter plans every request. It uses o200k_base, includes metadata and the longest question, and preserves disjoint target ownership. Context may overlap. The tokenizer is an estimate, not Jev’s tokenizer; provider failures and indivisible oversized chunks remain required.


Each prompt family is planned with its own question overhead. During development, independent questions with identical source states share a call; validation sends each finalist's exact question set. Exact payloads reused across window sizes are cached. Table “calls” means requests for one complete configuration, not the study’s shared-call total. Development billed tokens include any shared questions.


How the probability rules work
margin means p(insignificant) − max(p(significant), p(uncertain)). At a 0.70 threshold, a distribution of 0.90 / 0.05 / 0.05 passes; 0.70 / 0.20 / 0.10 does not. probability_times_confidence multiplies the exclusion probability by the Choice confidence (distribution concentration, not a correctness guarantee).
For category questions, max takes the largest yes probability. sum_clipped adds them and caps at 1; noisy_or uses 1 − product(1 − p). max_with_veto takes the smaller of max-category and 1 − p(requires review); review_complement uses that latter value alone.


Exact prompts and outcome definitions


How recursive splitting works — simplified
visit(hunk):
  if estimated_tokens(state + longest_question + overhead) ≤ window:
    keep hunk as one target
  else if a legal boundary exists near the token midpoint:
    visit(left); visit(right)
  else:
    leave this indivisible target for human review

For each fitting leaf:
  expand neighboring context while the token budget allows it
  judge only this leaf's target lines

How long does the evaluation take?


Wall time is measured around API execution and response recording, with concurrency recorded per phase above. Plan loading and verification are measured separately; tokenization/export, threshold scoring, report generation and pauses between phases are excluded. Request latency includes client serialization, HTTP, response validation, retries and backoff, but excludes time waiting for a worker. The 95th percentile uses the nearest-rank method.


The table below sums overlapping request durations: these sums are not elapsed wall time. Development calls can contain questions from multiple prompt configurations, so their latency is for the shared request. Validation sends each finalist's exact question set. Reused payloads count once per configuration; rows share observations and must not be added together.


Four workers is this experiment's client setting, not a measured optimum. TypeSafe documents 1,200 requests/minute and 250,000 tokens/second for Jev 1.13. Its throttling guidance recommends exponential backoff for HTTP 429 and 529. This runner retries 429 and selected 5xx codes, but does not yet handle 529 or server retry-delay headers. A higher-concurrency throughput study needs request/token pacing and that retry handling.

How much do larger windows save?
These are development measurements. Incomplete rows are sizing diagnostics, not candidates for the top ten. Many hunks already fit the smallest budget, so larger windows cannot reduce their one-request floor. Oversized targets send no request and receive no exclusion credit.


The worst approaches
These development configurations produced the most false-excluded cases, then lines. The examples preserve the actual source and returned scores. A separate agent rechecked all 31 distinct significant coordinates in the listed examples and confirmed genuine false exclusions; this bounded check does not cover every error counted in the aggregate. Summing category probabilities or using noisy-or is an experimental heuristic: the category judgments are not independent probabilities of disjoint events.

What this cannot establish
The labels are agent-authored under your policy, with syntax assistance and agent review, not independent human gold labels. Selection intentionally covers both positive and negative cases and larger hunks; prevalence is not a random estimate of ordinary reviews. Tests and lockfiles contribute many excluded lines. General generated files and other programming languages have little or no direct coverage.
This pass uses one observation per unique payload. Cached responses and correlated lines are not repetitions or independent samples. The top ten can overfit development; held-out results are shown separately. No production exclusion logic has changed, and response-driven uncertainty splitting was not evaluated here.
